Locations where typical pedestrian crossings are fewer are not in pedestrian recall and the button must be pressed to get a walk signal.  At large intersections with heavy traffic but few pedestrians  pedestrian recall  would cause all traffic to stop up to 40 seconds whether there was pedestrian actually waiting to cross the street or not.  This would cause undue delay to bicycles  buses  cars  trucks  and other modes of surface transportation.  It could also lead to driver frustration and a disregard to the traffic signal.  Putting a traffic signal is pedestrian recall in a low pedestrian area would be similar to pressing all the buttons on an elevator to stop at each floor  whether you wanted to stop on that floor or not.  That would lead to frustration using that elevator.    In the meantime during the shutdown  BTD is operating the online traffic signals at shorter off-peak cycle lengths which will reduce delays for all users.  As for the pedestrian buttons  we suggest you treat them as any other object in the public domain such as elevator buttons  doorknobs  etc.  Use your elbow  or the cuff of your sleeve to avoid touching the buttons directly with your hands.  Wash your hands frequently with soap and water  use hand sanitizer  and avoid touching your face in public.  Thanks.
